summary:
The Full-Day Argolis Tour travels from Athens into the northeastern Peloponnese, where some of ancient Greece’s most important archaeological sites are found. At Mycenae, explore the fortified citadel and remains of the civilization that dominated the region during the Late Bronze Age. The route also reaches Epidaurus, renowned for its remarkably preserved ancient theatre and long association with healing and the Sanctuary of Asclepius.
Everything is arranged as a single-day journey from Athens, with no hotel change required. Air-conditioned coach transportation, a professional guide and entrance fees for the scheduled visits are included, keeping the focus on exploring Argolis rather than managing travel logistics.

itinerary.title: Day Tour Argolis from Athens
itinerary.text: Depart from Athens via the coastal road along the Saronic Gulf to the Corinth Canal. Continue to Mycenae and visit the Lion Gate, Cyclopean Walls, and Royal Tombs. Proceed to Nafplio with views of the Palamidi Fortress. After lunch, continue to the Ancient Theatre of Epidaurus, famous for its remarkable acoustics. After the tour, return to Athens.

faqs.q: What is included in the Full Day Argolis Tour?
faqs.a: The Full Day Argolis Tour takes you through one of Greece's most historic regions in the northeastern Peloponnese. The excursion includes transportation from Athens, guided visits to the Corinth Canal, Mycenae, Nafplio, and Epidaurus, allowing visitors to discover some of the country's most important archaeological and cultural landmarks.

faqs.q: How much does the Full Day Argolis Tour cost?
faqs.a: The tour starts from €145 per person for the 2026 season. The price includes round-trip transportation, professional English-speaking guide services, and sightseeing according to the itinerary. Entrance fees and meals may vary depending on the package selected.

faqs.q: How long does the Full Day Argolis Tour last?
faqs.a: The tour lasts approximately 8 hours, including travel time from Athens. It is a full-day excursion designed to showcase the highlights of the Argolis region in a comfortable and well-organized itinerary

faqs.q: What are the main attractions visited during the tour?
faqs.a: Highlights typically include the Corinth Canal, the ancient city of Mycenae, the Lion Gate, the Tomb of Agamemnon, the picturesque town of Nafplio, and the Ancient Theatre of Epidaurus, famous for its exceptional acoustics and preservation.

faqs.q: Does the Full Day Argolis Tour include a guide?
faqs.a: Yes, professional English-speaking guides accompany the tour. Your guide will provide historical background, archaeological insights, and fascinating stories about the civilizations that shaped this important region of Greece.

faqs.q: Why is the Argolis region important in Greek history?
faqs.a: Argolis is home to some of Greece's most significant archaeological treasures. Mycenae was one of the most powerful centers of the Bronze Age Greek world, while Epidaurus became famous as a healing sanctuary and for its magnificent ancient theater.

faqs.q: How fit do I need to be for the tour?
faqs.a: The physical difficulty is moderate. Travelers should be comfortable walking through archaeological sites, climbing some steps, and navigating uneven terrain. Most visitors with average fitness levels can comfortably participate.

faqs.q: What should I wear for the Argolis Tour?
faqs.a: Comfortable walking shoes are highly recommended. During warmer months, visitors should bring sunscreen, sunglasses, a hat, and water. Light, comfortable clothing is ideal for exploring outdoor archaeological sites.

faqs.q: What is the cancellation policy for the Full Day Argolis Tour?
faqs.a: You can generally cancel free of charge up to 24 to 48 hours before the tour departure time, depending on the operator's policy. Cancellations made closer to departure may be subject to fees.

faqs.q: Is the Full Day Argolis Tour suitable for first-time visitors to Greece?
faqs.a: Yes, this tour is an excellent choice for first-time visitors interested in Greek history, mythology, and archaeology. It offers the opportunity to visit several of Greece's most famous historical sites in a single day while enjoying beautiful scenery and cultural experiences.
